## Dataset

The dataset is for patients part of the Mt. Sinai Millions (MSM) cohort, for each patient we have some demographic information and their "medical history".
The medical history is the list of ICD codes (specifiyng diagnoses) assigned to a patient by a doctor during a hospital visit for all recorded vists for that patient. So for every visit recorded we have the set of ICD codes assigned. 
We will turn this long-form medical history into a set of descriptive features for each patient that are better suited to linear modelling where patients are independent data points.
We also use the medical history to define the outcome we are studying for each patient and whether they experience SI, Broad SA or Narrow SA.

## Plot Patient Demographics

Load clean demographics data
```{r load_data}
# all_combined_data <- load_all_combined_data(force_redo=FALSE)
demographics_df <- 
    clean_demographics_data() %>% 
    # turn columns into neat factors, leaving NAs as NAs
    factorize_demographics_data() %>% 
    # remove all patients without complete demographic records
    filter(if_all(everything(), ~!is.na(.x))) %>%
    select(
        FID,
        current_age,

        is_religious,
        is_cisgender,
        is_married
    )
```
Plot individual distributions for all `r nrow(demographics_df)` patients with no missing data.
```{r plot_demographics, fig.dims=c(6, 8)}
make_single_ggbar <- function(col_name, plot_df=demographics_df){
    plot.obj <- 
        plot_df %>% 
        select(!!sym(col_name)) %>%
        count(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
        add_column(feature=col_name) %>%  # dummy x-axis
        mutate(pct=prop.table(n)) %>%  # counts to percentages
        arrange(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
        mutate(ypos=1 - (cumsum(pct) - pct/2)) %>%  # percentage label position on figure
        {
            ggplot(
                data=.,
                aes(
                    x=feature,
                    y=pct,
                    fill=.data[[col_name]],
                )
            ) + 
            geom_col(position='stack') +  # stacked bar plot
            geom_text(
                aes(
                    label=scales::percent(pct, accuracy=0.1),
                    y=ypos
                ),
                vjust=0.5,    # nudge above top of bar
                size = 3
            ) + 
            scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +
            guides(fill=guide_legend(ncol=1)) +
            theme_minimal() +
            theme(
                # axis.text.x=element_text(angle=55, vjust=1, hjust=1),
                # axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                legend.position='right',
                axis.title = element_blank()
            )
        }
}
current_age_dist <- 
    demographics_df %>% select(current_age) %>% add_column(feature='age') %>%
    {
        ggplot(
            aes(x=current_age),
            data=.
        ) + 
        geom_histogram(binwidth=1) +
        # coord_flip() +
        scale_y_continuous(labels=label_number(scale_cut=cut_short_scale())) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x=element_text(angle=55),
            axis.title.y=element_blank()
        )
    }
# make plot with patchwork
design <- "
CCAB
DEFG
"
{
    make_single_ggbar('gender')       +
    make_single_ggbar('ethnicity')    + 
    current_age_dist +
    make_single_ggbar('is_deceased')  +
    make_single_ggbar('is_religious') +
    make_single_ggbar('is_cisgender') +
    make_single_ggbar('is_married')   +
    plot_layout(design=design)
}
```

## Defining patient outcomes 

For every patinent we want to create a discrete output column that specifies what experience (if any) the patient had with Suicidal Ideation or Actions.
We have 3 lists of ICD codes, where if a patient has been assigned a code, they have the outcome for Ideation (SI), Broad Action (Broad SA) and Narrow Action (Narrow SA), and "control" if they dont match any codes across all lists.  
Using these lists of codes
Using the assigned ICD codes we can define these discrete columns in several other ways as  follows and test for differences in model construction. 

  - `Full`:  {"None", "SI", "Broad SA", "Narrow SA"}
  - `SI Only`:  {"None", "SI"}
  - `Any SI`:  {"None", "SI", "Broad SA", "Narrow SA"}
  - `Any SA`:  {"None", "Broad SA", "Narrow SA"}

*Note* that all encodings use the same set of samples, just changing the case/control labels.
We can also assign other phenotypes, such as Alcohol Use Disorder and Substance Use Disorder from the ICD codes in the same way.

## Featurizing Medical history

We have the history of when which ICD codes were assigned to each patient, so we can featurize this time series to get the following sets of values per patient.

### Capture "Shape" of History

Now we can add features derived from each patients medical history. 
Here the "history" is every time they were assigned a unique ICD code on a specific date,
so a 2-column tibble with the columns `encounter_date` and `ICD_code`. 
From such a table we can compute the following features and what they may represent to our models

| Feature Name | Definition | Interpretation |
|--------------|:-----------|:---------------|
 `n_codes` | total codes assigned (unique date + code) ||
 `n_unique_codes` | unique codes assigned |  how many conditions does the patient have? health "prior"? |
 `history_length` | time between first and most recent visit | extensive medical history? many conditions? access to healthcare? |
 `n_visits` |  number of unique visits recorded | same as length, but maybe better |
 `most_common_code` |  which code was assigned the most frequently to the patient | their longest known condition? (appears on multiple visits) |
 `most_common_code.freq` | how frequently the most common code was assigned out of all codes assigned | how long they've known about theyre longest known condition (# of visits |
`code_frequency` | n_codes / history_length | |

: How we featurize each patient's medical history {tbl-colwidth="[10,40,50]"}


- can compute a cumulative distribution over time i.e. number total codes assigned & number unique codes assigned
- burstiness: did the patient have a single encounter where they gained lots of codes? i.e. big medical change?
